label: prf:q-casimir-exists
title: Proof of existence of the $q$-Casimir element
html:
The formula C_q = FE + (qK + q^{-1}K^{-1} - (q + q^{-1}))/(q - q^{-1})^2 is a well-defined element of \mathcal{U}_q(\mathfrak{su}(2)) whenever (q - q^{-1}) is invertible in the ground ring R. Centrality is verified directly using the defining relations of \mathcal{U}_q(\mathfrak{su}(2)): the commutator [E, F] = (K - K^{-1})/(q - q^{-1}) and the K-relations KEK^{-1} = q^2 E, KFK^{-1} = q^{-2} F; the computation is standard (Kassel VI.4).

The eigenvalue on the spin-j irrep is computed by evaluating C_q on the highest-weight vector: K v_j = q^{2j} v_j and E v_j = 0 give C_q v_j = [j]_q[j+1]_q v_j after simplifying the K + K^{-1} term. Hence C_q|_{V_j} = [j]_q[j+1]_q \cdot \mathrm{id}.

Over \mathbb{F}_p, \mathbb{Q}_p, \mathbb{C}_p the same formula holds whenever (q - q^{-1}) is invertible in the base ring — a generic hypothesis excluding roots of unity of small order.
